meta.title: Bengaluru new domestic water connection grid-only re-score evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. This is a second, independently gathered row for Bengaluru, produced by the same method as the twelve city rows so that the pilot site is measured the way the comparison cities were; it does not reuse and did not read the deep pilot ledger for this service. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: every one of the board's published rate documents for a new connection is a one-page scan with no text layer, so no figure could be read from any of them; the board's own Know Your Connection Fees route returned a zero-byte file; the amount payable is computed inside the application after login, which was not crossed; a statement that the board's English-language route does not carry through to its contact and office-location pages was recorded during the pass, and the audit found it uncited under protocol section 7 because the ledger holds no source record for the corporate site those pages sit on; it is retained as a contested claim, supports no cell, and should not be read as an established finding; four of the five source URLs have no Wayback snapshot. Do not submit personal data through this ledger. One audit limitation ships unresolved: the corporate site's English landing page, contact information page and office location page were searched during the pass but have no source record in this ledger, which is why the claim that the English route did not carry through to those pages is retained as contested and supports no cell. The source record for the board's rate documents carries no publication date but does carry a visible-date note stating that none is shown on the route or on the files it links, so no source-date limitation remains open.

agencies.name: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board

scenarios.label: Bengaluru new domestic water connection
scenarios.summary: The individual owner of a built residential property with no connection applies to the city's water utility for a new domestic water supply, with sewer only where the same application covers it. Bulk or high-rise connections, commercial use, regularisation of unauthorised connections, name transfer on an existing account and tanker supply are excluded.

claims.text: The board publishes a toll-free number 1916 on its consumer routes for help or complaints or support related to a water connection application.

claims.text: The board's corporate site offers an English language route, and on the access date that route did not carry through to its contact information and office location pages, which rendered in Kannada.
claims.notes: Recorded as observed. It bears on whether an English-reading applicant can reach the office list; a Kannada-reading applicant may be able to. Audit 2026-09-06: the only cited source is source_bengaluru_grid_water_owc_portal, the Jaladhare consumer portal at owc.bwssb.gov.in, whose source record describes that portal's login, consumer manuals, important-documents and application-status routes; it does not cover the corporate site at bwssb.karnataka.gov.in or its contact and office-location pages, and the ledger holds no source record for those pages. The observation is retained and marked contested pending a source record for the pages actually observed, and it supports no expectation cell. No login was used, no OTP was requested and no personal data was entered.

The status routes beside it need no login, which is why the after-submission evidence does not rest on the gated surface. No login was used, no OTP was requested and no personal data was entered. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the boundary and the three surfaces behind it.

claims.text: What a resident owner pays for a new domestic water connection is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Part of the reason is a login boundary, and part is that the published documents cannot be read at all. No login was used, no OTP was requested and no personal data was entered. The three observed reasons behind this unknown are carried by sourced claims rather than by fragments of this one: every rate document is an unreadable scan (claim_bengaluru_grid_water_rate_documents_unreadable), the route that would give the total returns an empty file (claim_bengaluru_grid_water_know_your_fees_empty), and the computed amount appears only past the login (claim_bengaluru_grid_water_tentative_charges_after_entry and claim_bengaluru_grid_water_login_boundary_3).

claims.text: How long a new domestic water connection takes at any stage or in total is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related: the stage count is described in a public manual and carries no days. The observed reason is carried by claim_bengaluru_grid_water_status_shows_stage_and_officer_2, which records that the Status tab shows a count of stages completed.

claims.text: Which office or officer sanctions a new domestic water connection is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Partly login-related: the assigned officer is shown to the applicant past the boundary. No login was used, no OTP was requested and no personal data was entered. The two observed reasons behind this unknown are carried by sourced claims: the assigned-officer view sits past the login boundary (claim_bengaluru_grid_water_login_boundary_4), and the published contact routes give a helpline and a general contact document (claim_bengaluru_grid_water_toll_free_and_helpdesk and claim_bengaluru_grid_water_toll_free_and_helpdesk_2).
